plain: An official who checks the accounts of a government or business

webster.text: A hearer; one who attends to hear a discourse.

more.text: A person appointed and authorized to examine an account or accounts, compare the charges with the vouchers, examine the parties and witnesses, allow or reject charges, and state the balance.

example.quote: They may examine and pass all accounts of the State, relating either to the collection or expenditure of the revenue, or appoint auditors, to state and adjust the same.
example.cite: Md. Const. of 1776 and Declaration of Rights (Nov. 11, 1776)
